states.name: narrow
states.gap: No bottom gutter: the column runs off the window edge with 0px padding — the last line starts at y=1796 and is sliced mid-glyph by the 1800px boundary, where B holds its last line 36px clear of a rule. A also gives 2px less leading (74px pitch vs 76, ~1.71 vs ~1.76 at the same 43px glyph size) and wraps 6 characters earlier (56ch/1539px column vs 62ch/1620px), so the same passage costs more scrolling.
states.gapTheirs: Markdown markers sit inline instead of hanging, so the left edge breaks three times on one screen: body starts at x=142, but '# The Lighthouse' starts at 193 and '## What the sea keeps' at 217 — a 51–75px jog. A hangs '#' at 129 and '##' at 105 and lands every heading, body line and list item on the same 181px edge. B also crops the page: side margins 142/158px against A's 181/200, plus a title bar and a live '188 words / 961 characters / 1 min read' footer taking ~127px of vertical space.
states.verdict: Same paper, same type, same caret — the fight is entirely about the left edge and the frame, and A wins both. B's headings shove themselves 51 and 75 pixels to the right of the body edge, which is exactly the ragged column an editor is supposed to prevent, and it does it while a word counter sits under your sentence counting them. A's page is unbroken and unfurnished; its sin is running the text into the bottom edge with a half-line guillotined at the viewport boundary, which is untidy but not something you look at while composing. Six characters of measure and 2px of leading do not buy back a column that won't hold a straight line.

states.gap: Tighter vertical rhythm: line boxes are 74px vs A's 76px (≈1.62 vs ≈1.69 against ~22.6 CSS px type, ~13.7px advance), and it wraps ~2 characters earlier (~60ch vs A's ~62-63ch, longest ink run 1629px vs 1633px). Over a four-line paragraph B's block closes up ~8px more than A's.
states.gapTheirs: Ragged left edge: A's '#' sits inline at x=622 so the heading's first word starts at x=673, while body text starts at x=623 — a 50px (25 CSS px, exactly one mono advance) step in the column's left edge. B hangs the marker out at x=571-594 and lands heading text at x=623, flush with the body, so the measure's left edge never moves.
states.verdict: A's page has one flaw you cannot unsee: type a heading and the text column's left edge kicks 25px right, because the '#' is parked inside the measure instead of hanging outside it. B pays 1px per line of leading for a left margin that stays true through headings and paragraphs alike, and that is the trade every book compositor makes. Everything else is a photocopy — same paper hex, same 3px caret, same dimmed marker, same two-line paragraph gap — so A has nothing to buy its way out with. Two percent more air does not compensate for a margin that wobbles on every H1.
